title: The Torah: a five-book fold
author: Jonathan Sacks
sourceLocator: Introduction, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 14); discussion pp. 6–8
note: A whole-book proposal, not a verse-by-verse alignment. The five book units are Sacks’s published outline. Full-book verse ranges are ChiFold reading-context expansions using the displayed edition. Sacks describes the broader Sinai movement as extending beyond Leviticus into late Exodus and early Numbers; the diagram’s central unit is Leviticus.

groups.label: A
groups.title: Genesis looks toward Israel’s beginnings; Deuteronomy looks toward its life ahead, framing the central journey and covenant.
groups.sourceClaim: Genesis looks toward Israel’s beginnings; Deuteronomy looks toward its life ahead, framing the central journey and covenant.

groups.label: B
groups.title: Exodus carries Israel toward Sinai; Numbers carries it away toward the land. Sacks compares the journeys, recurring complaints and demands on Moses.

groups.label: C
groups.title: Leviticus occupies the middle book position, focusing the five-book outline on Israel’s life with God at Sinai.
